item.title: When AI Joins Educational Inquiry, What Should Remain Human?
item.description: A playful, dramatized interview with a fictional research correspondent synthesizing five studies about AI-assisted qualitative analysis, educational ethics, and teacher-facing learning analytics. This is not an actual interview with any author.
item.content:encoded:
A playful, dramatized interview with a fictional research correspondent synthesizing five studies about AI-assisted qualitative analysis, educational ethics, and teacher-facing learning analytics. The guest is fictional; the dialogue paraphrases the research and is not an actual author interview.

Sources

  1. Xiner Liu et al. (2025), Qualitative Coding with GPT-4: Where it Works Better. Zotero · DOI
  2. Kien Nguyen-Trung (2025), ChatGPT in thematic analysis: Can AI become a research assistant in qualitative research? Zotero · DOI
  3. Rudolf Messner, Samuel Smith, and Carol Richards (2025), Artificial Intelligence and Qualitative Data Analysis: Epistemological Incongruences and the Future of the Human Experience. Zotero · DOI
  4. Edward Dieterle, Chris Dede, and Michael Walker (2022), The cyclical ethical effects of using artificial intelligence in education. Zotero · DOI
  5. Chao Yang (2025), Chat-LAD: Enhancing Teacher Understanding of Learning Analytics Dashboard with AI-Empowered Explanations. Zotero
